document.abstract: When a flashlamp is required to flash at high rates, the charging circuit is required to supply more current. Eventually, a condition arises where the flashlamp does not deionize but goes into a continuous arc that is called “holdover.” Conditions for the limiting frequency in terms of circuit and lamp volt-ampere characteristics are given. Experimental data on several flashlamps are presented. Circuits which force a flashlamp to operate at high frequency even if it does not deionize are discussed.
